title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: 3D Technology Empowers the Traditional Apparel Foreign Trade Industry
description: Review of CLO Academic Month 2024! A conversation with Ms. Shao Linlin from Guangdong Textile Import and Export Co., Ltd., introducing the role of 3D technology in the apparel foreign trade industry, including helping companies save on samples, reduce costs, promote sustainable development, simplify communication processes, and replace photo displays to showcase clothing on e-commerce platforms.
transcript:
Today, I’m going to share with you how 3D technology supports our traditional trade industry.  
First, I will share my thoughts on four aspects.  
The first is an introduction to Guangdong Provincial Law.  
The second is the promotion and impact of 3D clothing on trade.  
The third is the presentation of 3D products to our colleagues and the outlook for the future.  

Guangdong Provincial Law was established in 1949.  
As I mentioned earlier, we are a state-owned enterprise and the first to engage in foreign trade in the clothing industry in South China.  
We have more than 500 fabric factories and over 200 cotton factories.  
We serve as the vice-chairman of the China Provincial Exports and Imports Association.  
Tongzhuang and Niuzai are leading companies in China.  
Our company produced the first jeans exported from China.  
We have branches in many locations including the United States, Singapore, Shanghai, and Ireland.  

Our company has been using 3D technology for a relatively long time.  
We began using 3D in 2008 because the company’s leadership foresaw its future applications.  
Initially, we used Optex with TD3 software.  
Later, in 2018, we started using CLO, which was a comprehensive upgrade.  
We have also adopted more well-known 3D software in the industry.  
Our team has been continuously expanding, and we have obtained various related certifications from major customers.  

Here is a demonstration of 3D. From 2017 to 2023, we have observed changes between 3D samples and physical samples.  
Our physical samples have steadily decreased, while 3D samples have continuously increased.  
All kinds of customers have been using 3D samples.  
Since 2008, the use of 3D samples has grown significantly.  
In 2019, due to the pandemic, the usage of 3D samples accelerated rapidly.  
Although our clothing industry was not able to open during the pandemic, it did not stop operating.  
Therefore, we adopted virtual avatars.  
We ensured that physical samples could not be sent out, but virtual samples continued without interruption, allowing production to proceed smoothly.  

Here, we compare 3D samples with traditional samples.  
3D online research and development has been compressed to 3 to 7 days.  
In the traditional industry, it takes 15 to 60 days from start to finish.  
This significantly reduces the time and also compresses and lowers costs.  
As a result, our use of 3D technology is increasing.  

3D has played a role in promoting our clothing industry.  
Currently, the industry is consumer-driven, with declining consumer purchasing power and many new customers who are experience-oriented consumers.  
Our brand faces high inventory pressure and environmental and social responsibility challenges.  
Originally, the brand relied on large orders, but now orders have decreased to smaller batches.  
There is market prejudice and an increasingly conservative attitude.  
Consequently, competition among foreign trade companies is becoming more internalized.  

As the global economy integrates further, the Chinese foreign trade industry faces many challenges requiring continuous innovation and breakthroughs.  
So how do we improve the competitiveness of our companies to cope with market changes and competitive pressure?  
3D technology offers a new path.  
It shortens our development cycle and reduces costs, providing a breakthrough.  
It allows our designers to present samples from design to final product faster, becoming a new channel for us to stand out.  

3D clearly reduces sample costs, physical logistics costs, and overall development stage expenses.  
3D also optimizes our entire inventory since sample piles require space; now we can store samples digitally in 3D, saving storage costs and improving efficiency and cost control.  
This enhances our competitiveness and strengthens foreign trade companies’ international market capabilities.  

Environmental protection is a hot topic today.  
Using 3D can reduce material waste and aligns better with environmental protection concepts.  
In sample production, cotton waste is inevitable, especially since samples rarely pass on the first try, causing further waste.  
3D helps us be more environmentally friendly, reflecting our company’s social responsibility.  

3D technology can break through major obstacles.  
Often, as mentioned earlier, physical 3D samples cannot be sent out, but with 3D, I can send an email and present a 360-degree view to customers.  
Unlike before, when selling to customers required carrying large and small physical samples, which was often impractical, 3D allows us to use one model to showcase different fabrics and colors more effectively.  

Through 3D, we can attract new customers, especially young consumers who demand high-tech and novel experiences.  
Combined with social media and online marketing, 3D products increase user interaction and brand exposure on the internet.  

This product’s advantage is low cost because it saves logistics and physical sample costs, as well as expenses related to production machines and spaces.  
Previously, we had to wait a long time for physical samples.  
Now, from fabric production to sample creation, it is fast and simple, taking only about two hours, or at most one to two days, and is easy to modify.  

With traditional clothing, simple parts can be modified, but large parts are often wasted.  
3D samples can be adjusted or modified anytime and also serve as samples.  
Communication with customers is more convenient, and more variations can be shown.  
Later, I will show you the richness of our 3D samples, which use different forms to better showcase products and improve interaction with customers and consumers.  

All our 3D data can be digitized effectively, allowing us to collect and utilize it for development.  
The environment remains a key concern worldwide.  

Next, we will showcase some 3D products from our team.  
Typically, our customers have similar needs, but due to different knowledge and store settings, they need to present products in various ways.  
We have a 3D store to display our clothes with features like hanging, flat shoes, folding effects, and wool fabric effects.  
These are our bullfrogs.  
Next to it is a physical sample and a 3D sample.  
The 3D sample is excellent; I don’t need a hardener to open a mold but can show 3D models that realistically represent the product to customers.  
If customers need to change patterns or designs, it is very fast.  
The denim styles are consistent, and customers can preview all kinds of washing effects to confirm if it meets their expectations.  

Here is a comparison between the real product and 3D.  
Previously, we had some difficulties upfront, but now we can basically see the sample effect in advance.  
This is a sweater where we can see the texture from the original fabric to the created sweater and make recommendations to customers.  

Currently, we have many jumpers.  
For example, I made a traditional chicken horse garment.  
When making jumpers, I can use 3D.  
Jumpers are basically riding horses; normally, we need many sample pieces, but with 3D, we save a lot of sample-making costs.  

We also use some products in different scenarios and configurations at home.  
Our team often showcases our work in fairs.  
Previously, we needed to produce many physical products, but now we can quickly use designers’ ideas to display overall design effects.  

Additionally, we have created some VR booths, which we find relatively useful now.  
Traditionally, we needed a real person to try on clothing to test comfort.  
Because we specialize in coats, and if the wearer is a child who goes to school, it was necessary to book a model, which was difficult.  
Now, we use a 3D model to test fit and movement.  
We also use AI to quickly change makeup, skin color, and effects.  
For example, for client groups in Europe and the United States, I can switch the model to represent different faces to match the client group, saving photo shoot costs and accelerating e-commerce applications.  

These are some of the styles we started with.  
We can quickly use AI and 3D for pre-sales without matching physical samples.  

What about the future outlook?  
I believe continuous software optimization is what our company expects.  
CLO has always been committed to updating software and cooperating actively with us, and we are grateful for this partnership.  

Another focus is optimizing technologies such as AI and big data.  
We are very pleased with these technologies and will use them to make 3D design more intelligent and automated.  
In the future, we will use VR and AR to better showcase virtual samples and popularize them in the metaverse.  

Pre-sale predictions include 3D design and general applications in the clothing industry.  
I believe 3D design will become a standard tool in the clothing industry, greatly advancing its digital transformation.  

Currently, like our company, before developing a sample, we first test the fabric.  
Modeling is not difficult for us now, but matching it to the real fabric is what we are trying to improve.  
In the future, we may increase the use of 3D fabrics, which will greatly enhance 3D applications.  

3D technology will also become part of the standard process for 3D outerwear because, as everyone knows, our outerwear is much better than 3D fabric.  
We also require more flexible and efficient cross-border e-commerce, which will benefit from 3D technology.  

We are also undergoing a comprehensive upgrade of the manufacturing industry.  
Currently, we use intelligent production.  
In the future, 3D will replace paper patterns.  
We use 3D extensively now; when styles and craftsmanship are confirmed digitally, physical samples are no longer necessary.  
After 3D approval, minor modifications can be made, and production can proceed directly.  

Regarding employment impact, I believe it will mostly affect some designers.  
3D is very helpful because after designers create styles, the original effect is two-dimensional, but transforming it into 3D allows them to see results more directly.  

New job opportunities will emerge in 3D cloud technology.  
I believe this expertise will become a new profession, opening new roles such as 3D consultants and 3D printers.  

Training and education are important.  
Yesterday and today, several professors and teachers shared extensively and recognized the importance of education and 3D.  
I believe talents will continue to emerge.  

Our foreign trade enterprises need to attract customer and market attention.  
In product design and display, we need greater competitiveness.  
3D talents can use their skills to innovate new products, models, and promotional materials.  
This enables companies to better showcase and promote products.  

The foreign trade industry also needs 3D talents to quickly develop and manufacture products using 3D and other technologies.  
This helps companies improve productivity, quality, and reduce costs.  

3D talents can create impressive visual effects and animations for product promotion, videos, advertisements, and shows.  
In a fiercely competitive market, such visual presentations help companies attract more potential clients.  

As virtual reality matures and real-time technologies develop rapidly, foreign trade enterprises will increasingly use these technologies to display and promote products.  
3D talents can build virtual scenes and interactive experiences to provide a better shopping and product experience.  

For example, our company creates men’s and women’s clothing and can show different exhibition halls.  
Every season, we update products to better present our diverse offerings to customers.  

From our company’s perspective, we summarize our needs for 3D talents.  
Of course, those skilled in 3D modeling software can independently complete 3D modeling and modifications.  

In fact, many 3D talents we recruited before still have some gaps and need assistance from pattern masters.  
After building the 3D model, modifications are often necessary, requiring repeated work by the pattern master.  

In the future, I believe 3D modeling will require more knowledge of how CAD software is created, verified, and how to modify clothing designs.  
We also need to use more design software related to PSAI to process patterns.  
Additionally, software like CSD and Maya can be used to visualize and optimize overall animations.  

When recruiting talents, our TD (Technical Development) department focuses more on sample examination.  
New recruits first learn about clothing craftsmanship and structure, then clothing design, and finally 3D.  
This will make our 3D talents more comprehensive.  

3D samples produced can better meet customer standards.  
Therefore, 3D talents need to be familiar with clothing craftsmanship and production techniques.  

In school, we mainly focus on 3D appearance and design effects and participate in various competitions.  
Our company, however, requires 3D for clothing not only on the outside but also detailed craftsmanship that simulates real samples.  

Thus, all craftsmanship and production require more knowledgeable 3D personnel.  

Also, since we are a foreign trade company, good English skills related to clothing are necessary for reading, writing, and listening.  

For our company, 3D talents should not only be able to model but also go further—engaging directly with customers, using professional language to recommend and sell products.  

We hope our staff have innovative and teamwork spirits, a love of learning and experiencing, and a strong sense of responsibility.  
They should have good communication skills and be able to handle difficult projects and the associated risks and responsibilities.  

They should understand and anticipate knowledge and technology needs and be able to expand channels.  

Our company is a good platform to help young people continue learning and improving.  

So our company embarks on a new journey, with new dreams, a new start, and new breakthroughs.  
We gather people from all over the world to join our business.  
We hope more people will join us.  

Thank you.

chunks.title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: 3D Technology Empowers the Traditional Apparel Foreign Trade Industry
chunks.content: ## Introduction to Guangdong Provincial Law and Company Background This section outlines the historical and organizational context of Guangdong Provincial Law and its role in China’s traditional apparel foreign trade industry, highlighting key company facts and industry positioning. Guangdong Provincial Law was established in 1949. The company discussed is a state-owned enterprise and the first in South China to engage in foreign trade within the clothing industry. It operates with a strong industrial base, including over 500 fabric factories and more than 200 cotton factories. The company serves as the vice-chairman of the China Provincial Exports and Imports Association. Notable industry leaders such as Tongzhuang and Niuzai are mentioned as leading companies in China. This company produced the first jeans exported from China and maintains branches in the United States, Singapore, Shanghai, and Ireland. ## Adoption and Evolution of 3D Technology in Apparel Trade This section covers the company’s timeline and strategic adoption of 3D technology, including software used, team development, and certification achievements. The company began using 3D technology in 2008, initially adopting Optex with TD3 software. In 2018, the company upgraded to CLO software, known for its comprehensive 3D garment design capabilities. Additional industry-leading 3D software has also been integrated. Since the beginning, the 3D team has expanded and obtained various certifications required by major customers, ensuring compliance and expertise. ## Impact of 3D Samples on Product Development and Trade Efficiency This section explains the shift from physical to 3D samples, highlighting time and cost savings, pandemic-related adaptations, and customer acceptance. From 2017 to 2023, the company observed a steady decrease in physical samples and a corresponding increase in 3D samples. The use of 3D samples accelerated significantly during the 2019 pandemic when physical sample distribution was restricted. Virtual avatars and digital samples allowed uninterrupted production despite factory closures. 3D online research and development cycles have been compressed to 3 to 7 days, compared to traditional cycles of 15 to 60 days. This reduction in development time significantly lowers costs and increases flexibility. Customers across various segments have adopted 3D samples, reflecting widespread industry acceptance. ## Benefits of 3D Technology for the Traditional Apparel Industry This section details the comprehensive advantages of 3D technology, including cost reduction, inventory optimization, environmental benefits, and marketing enhancements. 3D technology reduces sample production costs, physical logistics expenses, and overall development costs. Digitally storing samples reduces warehouse needs and optimizes inventory management, enhancing cost control and operational efficiency. Environmental benefits arise from reduced material waste, especially cotton, which is commonly lost during traditional sample making due to multiple iterations. The company emphasizes social responsibility through this eco-friendly approach. 3D technology also enables remote sample presentation, replacing the need to physically transport multiple samples. A single 3D model can showcase different fabrics, colors, and washing effects, increasing customer engagement and reducing logistical challenges. Furthermore, 3D products appeal particularly to younger, tech-savvy consumers by combining with social media and online marketing to boost brand exposure and user interaction.

chunks.content: Environmental benefits arise from reduced material waste, especially cotton, which is commonly lost during traditional sample making due to multiple iterations. The company emphasizes social responsibility through this eco-friendly approach. 3D technology also enables remote sample presentation, replacing the need to physically transport multiple samples. A single 3D model can showcase different fabrics, colors, and washing effects, increasing customer engagement and reducing logistical challenges. Furthermore, 3D products appeal particularly to younger, tech-savvy consumers by combining with social media and online marketing to boost brand exposure and user interaction. ## Practical Applications and Demonstrations of 3D Garments This section provides examples of 3D product displays, virtual fitting, and sample comparisons, illustrating 3D’s practical use in apparel development and marketing. The company showcases 3D stores featuring garments with detailed effects such as hanging, flat shoes, folding, and wool fabric textures. Physical samples and their 3D counterparts are compared, showing high fidelity and faster modifiability without the need for physical molds. Denim products benefit from 3D previews of washing effects, while sweaters demonstrate realistic fabric textures from raw material to finished garment. Jumpers, traditionally requiring many physical samples, achieve significant cost savings through 3D sample creation. The company also uses 3D technology to simulate different usage scenarios and configurations, facilitating rapid presentation of new designs at trade fairs without producing numerous physical samples. ## Integration of VR, AI, and Customization in Apparel Design This section discusses the incorporation of virtual reality (VR), artificial intelligence (AI), and customization technologies to improve fitting, marketing, and client-specific presentations. VR booths enable virtual fitting and comfort testing without real models, addressing challenges such as booking child models for school coats. AI allows rapid adjustments of makeup, skin color, and facial features on 3D avatars to better represent diverse client groups, reducing the need for costly photoshoots and speeding up e-commerce deployment. AI and 3D integration facilitate pre-sales activities, eliminating the dependency on physical samples and enabling faster customer engagement. ## Future Outlook: Software Development and Industry Trends This section forecasts the ongoing development of 3D design software, AI integration, and emerging technologies such as VR, AR, and metaverse applications within the clothing industry. The company expects continuous software optimization, particularly through its partnership with CLO, which actively updates and collaborates on improvements. Advanced technologies such as AI and big data will drive smarter, more automated 3D design processes. VR and AR will enhance virtual sample presentations and are anticipated to become mainstream in metaverse environments. 3D design is predicted to become a standard industry tool, accelerating the digital transformation within apparel manufacturing and trade. ## Enhancements in Fabric Modeling and Digital Manufacturing Processes This section covers improvements in fabric simulation, the replacement of traditional paper patterns with digital 3D processes, and intelligent production upgrades. While 3D modeling itself is mature, matching digital models accurately to real fabric characteristics remains a focus. Increasing the use of 3D fabric simulations will enhance the precision of virtual garments.

chunks.title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: 3D Technology Empowers the Traditional Apparel Foreign Trade Industry
chunks.content: 3D design is predicted to become a standard industry tool, accelerating the digital transformation within apparel manufacturing and trade. ## Enhancements in Fabric Modeling and Digital Manufacturing Processes This section covers improvements in fabric simulation, the replacement of traditional paper patterns with digital 3D processes, and intelligent production upgrades. While 3D modeling itself is mature, matching digital models accurately to real fabric characteristics remains a focus. Increasing the use of 3D fabric simulations will enhance the precision of virtual garments. The manufacturing industry is undergoing comprehensive upgrades, with intelligent production methods increasingly adopted. 3D technology is expected to replace paper patterns entirely, enabling direct production after digital approval and minor modifications. ## Employment Impact and Emerging Roles in 3D Apparel Technology This section analyzes the impact of 3D technology on employment, new professional opportunities, and the skills needed for the evolving apparel trade workforce. 3D technology primarily affects designers by enabling visualization of their work in 3D, improving design accuracy and communication. New job categories will emerge, including 3D consultants and 3D printer operators. Education and training are critical; professors and industry experts emphasize the importance of cultivating 3D talent. Foreign trade enterprises require 3D professionals capable of innovating product design, promotional materials, and manufacturing processes to enhance competitiveness. ## Skills and Competencies Required for 3D Talents in Apparel Trade This section details the technical and soft skills necessary for 3D professionals, including software proficiency, craftsmanship knowledge, language abilities, and customer interaction capabilities. 3D talents should be proficient in software such as CLO, CAD, PSAI, CSD, and Maya for modeling, pattern processing, and animation visualization. A deep understanding of clothing craftsmanship and production techniques is essential to produce 3D samples that meet customer standards. English proficiency related to the apparel industry is important for communication, documentation, and customer engagement. Beyond technical skills, 3D professionals should demonstrate innovation, teamwork, a passion for learning, responsibility, and strong communication skills to manage complex projects and client relationships effectively. ## Company’s Strategy for Developing 3D Talent and Industry Vision This section outlines the company’s approach to training 3D talent, integrating traditional clothing knowledge with digital skills, and fostering ongoing learning and innovation. New recruits in the Technical Development (TD) department start by learning clothing craftsmanship and structure, followed by clothing design, and then 3D software skills, creating well-rounded professionals. The company emphasizes that 3D design must simulate real samples, not only in appearance but also in detailed craftsmanship, requiring knowledgeable personnel. The company positions itself as a platform supporting continuous learning and professional growth, inviting talents worldwide to join its innovative journey and contribute to new breakthroughs. --- This document synthesizes insights on how 3D technology empowers the traditional apparel foreign trade industry through digital transformation, efficiency improvements, environmental benefits, and talent development.
